messages:
tara: Kickstarting a slightly different proof-of-isolation plan for an airgapped/private deploy. Main objectives: minimal provisioner RBAC, deny-by-default egress, signed audit envelopes, and an independent egress-fuzz test to demonstrate isolation under stress. Thoughts?

kishore: Love the egress-fuzzer idea. It provides negative testing: spawn synthetic pods that attempt a wide range of outbound calls and verify netpols + gateway block them. We should run it in canary only.

yuna: Agreed. Also note a new vuln: keystore-proxy v2.0.0 has CVE-2026-0705 (path-traversal in artifact fetch). Block rollout until v2.0.2. Preflight must include image-scan + SBOM.

tara: Plan sketch: 1) ensure image-scan & SBOM gates 2) deploy kms-gateway/kms-proxy in control ns 3) create provisioner-min ClusterRole and bind in canary ns only 4) apply deny-everywhere egress netpol with explicit allows to kms-proxy + monitoring 5) run egress-fuzzer for 10m 6) collect signed audit batch and evidence bundle 7) rotate ephemeral wrap keys.

kishore: Example ClusterRole I'll create for canary (avoid in-place patch):
```yaml
apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1
kind: ClusterRole
metadata:
  name: provisioner-minimal-canary
rules:
- apiGroups: [""]
  resources: ["pods","secrets"]
  verbs: ["get","list"]
```

yuna: Netpol snippet (deny egress except kms-proxy + prometheus):
```yaml
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: deny-egress-except-kms-proxy
spec:
  podSelector: {}
  policyTypes: ["Egress"]
  egress:
  - to:
    - namespaceSelector:
        matchLabels:
          app: kms-proxy
    - ipBlock:
        cidr: 10.10.0.0/24 # monitoring
```

tara: Egress-fuzzer behaviour: create 50 tiny pods that try TCP/UDP to random ports and known KMS endpoints. The verifier should assert "no connection to non-allowlist" and capture a small pcap-like proof for any failure.

kishore: For signed audit batches: we hash the ndjson stream, sign with HSM or customer KMS (mTLS), include key fingerprint + timestamp, and write to immutable bucket. TTL for ephemeral wrap keys: 7 days.

yuna: Operational hooks: if fuzzer finds unexpected egress, auto-isolate offending pod, collect conn metadata + signed tail of audit.log, rotate wrap keys, and open an incident. We should also capture the command that triggered the traffic for reproducibility.

ops-bot: Incident created INC-2026-111 for keystore-proxy upgrade (owner: yuna).

sec-oncall: Two minor asks: (1) ensure metrics sidecars are allowed to prometheus IPs so we don't break observability; (2) verify TLS-fingerprints for customer KMS endpoints are pre-registered.

tara: Good call. We'll annotate the metrics sidecar namespace to allow prometheus scrape CIDR, and require customers to provide KMS endpoint fingerprints or run our local HSM connector (binds to localhost).

yuna: Rollback plan: unbind canary ClusterRoleBinding, remove netpols, revert proxy image, revoke ephemeral keys, and destroy fuzzer pods. Keep steps scripted.

kishore: Canary window: 04:00 UTC. Checklist I'll own: [image-scan pass, deploy kms-proxy v2.0.2, apply provisioner-min role/binding, apply netpols, run egress-fuzzer 10m, collect signed audit bundle, publish artifact]. Who can be oncall?

tara: I can be oncall.

yuna: I'll watch signatures + vulnerability gate.

kishore: Thanks — I'll post the artifact permalink and a short attestation after the run.

tara: Sweet. If fuzzer finds anything we treat it as high-sev until proven otherwise. Tagging @sec-oncall for visibility.
